review: 2:1–2:5 הוֹי מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד … כֶּעָנִי וְנִבְזֶה — Psalm 24:7 (מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד) with 2 Cor 8:9 (הֶעֱנִי) and Isa 53:3 (נִבְזֶה); the Arabic يَا مَلِيكَ الْمَجْدِ … كَالْفَقِيرِ وَالْمُهَان is that combination, and Hebrew keeps both the royal title and the poverty.

3:1–3:2 חֶרְפָּה מְכַלָּה / חֲמַת מִשְׁפָּט נוֹרָא — the Arabic الْعَارَ الْمُذِيب / غَضَبَ الْعَدْلِ الرَّهِيب is 'consuming shame' and 'dread wrath of justice', the same pair as hymns 81 and 114; Hebrew keeps the participle מְכַלָּה to hold 'consuming'.
3:3 טָעַמְתָּ מָוֶת — Hebrews 2:9 (יִטְעַם מָוֶת); the Arabic ذُقْتَ الْمَوْتَ is that verb, and טָעַם is its fixed Hebrew equivalent.

3:5 וַתַּחְטֹף הַנֶּפֶשׁ מִתּוֹךְ הַלַּהַב — the Arabic فَاخْتَطَفْتَ النَّفْسَ مِنْ جَوْفِ اللَّهِيب is 'You snatched the soul from the midst of the flame'; חָטַף is the verb of snatching used for the rapture (hymns 98, 119), and לַהַב is the poetic flame (Isa 13:8).

1:3 שַׁנּוּהוּ — 'repeat it'; the Arabic رَدِّدُوهُ is the command to say the Lord's kindness over again, and שָׁנָה in the sense of repeating is biblical (Esth 3:4 uses it of saying a thing again and again).
